name: a-window-resize-under-the-panel-grabs-the-window
description:
The floating panel is a child window and takes every event over its own frame, so the only thing that keeps the window's resize border reachable while the panel is up is the band ApplyBounds leaves uncovered: kOverlayHorizontalInset points of the window along the docked edge. That band used to be 8 points wide and is now 5, which is thin enough that a hit-test question becomes a real one.

The reading is the panel's own screenX. The panel tracks the parent through ApplyBounds, so a drag that grabbed the WINDOW moves it, and a drag the panel swallowed leaves it exactly where it was. A press inside the band cannot resize the panel either way - .ovresize sits at the panel's trailing edge, not its leading one - so a number that did not move names the dead zone rather than some other outcome.

The pointer is already at the edge when the press lands, which is the state OnStripEntered refuses to reveal into. That is the point: the panel is up from the move before it, and the press must reach past it.
